cells.tense: The strength that builds and holds is here, and it is working as it is meant to.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: When someone brings you something heavy, sit with them and leave the repair alone until they ask for it.
cells.core:
You build things that last, and today that strength is doing what it is meant to do. Someone hands you something heavy and you don't flinch or reach for a tool — you stay, and it sits heavy between the two of you, and your not flinching is what lets them feel the whole of it. That is being with someone without disappearing into them: you are right there, and you are still yourself. That is the thing to keep feeding — the staying, not the fixing.

So when someone hands you something hard, let the repair wait. Stay with what they brought. If they want the tool, they will ask, and you will still be the one who builds — just not in the first minutes of their pain.
cells.sheetLine: You can be beside someone without reaching for a fix.
cells.place: beside someone who is hurting and does not want fixing

cells.tense: A fair call about a feeling has already been made before the feeling has finished arriving.
cells.act: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished
cells.ask: Let one feeling about someone run its course before you decide about it, then weigh one real exchange and leave that judgment where it lands.
cells.core:
You feel what other people feel, and the fairness has gotten there first. You know what would be just before anything has happened, you have already weighed what a word will cost them, and the weighing is standing where the being-with used to be. That care run this hard gets heavy for the person on the other end — they can feel the audit in your kindness.

Bring it back by letting a feeling run its course. Feel first. Decide after. One look, one time, one real exchange weighed, and then let it rest. If the same thing is still true next week, it will still be there to look at.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is getting there before the moment does.
cells.place: beside someone who is hurting and does not want fixing

cells.tense: The strength that builds and holds is standing at a door that has already closed.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Set down what you are still carrying from one finished thing in a relationship, and keep only what is actually still ahead of you.
cells.core:
You keep things standing, and the strength is being spent on something that has already ended. Someone comes close and you brace against an old arrangement, hold a position nobody is asking you to hold, and the connection does not quite land. The strength is real. What you are doing with it has nowhere to go anymore.

Let one finished thing be finished. Whatever you are still carrying from it — the shape of an old pact, a stance you took and have not put down — you can set it aside, and the step forward will be there when you do. You do not have to earn your way back in. You can just show up.
cells.sheetLine: The strength is real, and it is holding onto something finished.
cells.place: beside someone who is hurting and does not want fixing

cells.tense: The strength that steadies other people is doing its work without your name on it.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Ask someone you trust a plain question about where the two of you might head, and let their answer settle before you decide anything.
cells.core:
There is a strength in how you hold other people, and it operates without your name attached. You make it safe to say the hard thing, you keep the demand off the person across from you, and if anybody asked, you would say that's just what anyone does. The steadying in this belongs to you. You don't see it that way.

Let it be visible by asking instead of already knowing. A question is a small thing to set down in front of someone — a real one, nothing behind it — and what they say back will show you that you know how to be there without already holding the shape of where it should go. You don't have to claim it. You can ask.
cells.sheetLine: The steadying here belongs to you, and you file it under being easy to be around.
cells.place: beside someone who is hurting and does not want fixing
